newsitem.title: CHINA: China launches integrated circuit project.
newsitem.headline: China launches integrated circuit project.

text.p: China has launched its largest integrated circuit development project, part of the country's efforts to become a world leader in electronics, Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The agency said Premier Li Peng attended a ceremony in the Pudong development zone on Thursday to launch the "Project 909", which involves investment of more than 10 billion yuan.

"The project is the most wide-ranging ever launched in China's electronics sector. It will build a high-capacity production line to turn out each month 20,000 chips that are each 0.5 microns thick and eight inches long," the agency said.
An IC production line will be set up and several IC design companies launched as part of the project, it said.

The agency said China's IC industry suffers from low productivity and inadequate design capabilities. Domestic-made IC chips are at their thinnest one micron, compared with the 0.35-micron standard in the developed world, the agency said.

The annual output of the entire industry can meet only 20 percent of the country's market demand, making it necessary for China to import more than 10 billion yuan-worth of IC chips annually, it said.
Official estimates put China's annual IC demand by the end of the century at four billion chips with a combined value of 60 to 80 billion yuan.

"Project 909 will help China raise the annual output of integrated circuits to between one and 1.5 billion chips by the year 2000, and to increase the sales volume to 10 billion yuan, accounting for 30 percent of the home markets," the agency said.
